title: Disentanglement as Identifiable Pushforward Factorisation
claim: Unstructured latent posteriors leave axis traversals off the data's natural factor paths; axis-aligned posteriors make traversals follow independent factors.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, left-to-right, latent space mapped to data space by arrow
description: Two side-by-side panels with the same structure. Each shows a 2-D latent space Z with axes z1 and z2, drawn with light-blue ellipses for posteriors q(z|x). A black arrow labelled d points to a gray curve for the data manifold X, with M_d below it. In the left panel the ellipses are tilted at arbitrary angles. The blue singular-vector path wanders, and the green axis-traversal arrow is horizontal. Its image on the manifold (green dashed) drifts away from the red dashed seam. In the right panel the ellipses are axis-aligned and the blue path is horizontal. The green traversal image lies on top of the red seam. Blue, green and red dashed arrows carry the argument, and the labels sit next to them.
caption: Disentanglement illustrated for VAEs with full vs diagonal posteriors: Right singular vectors vi ∈Z of the decoder’s Jacobian (blue arrows) define (s.v.) paths in latent space (dashed blue); left singular vectors ui (red arrows) define seams in data space (dashed red). 1-D densities over seams factorise the manifold density pµ. (left) For VAEs with full posteriors, s.v. paths are arbitrary, hence the image of an axis-traversal (green) need not follow a seam. (right) For VAEs with diagonal posteriors, s.v. paths are axis-aligned, hence axis traversal images follow seams, over which 1-D densities are independent factors of pµ, achieving disentanglement, (D1).
abstract: We characterise disentanglement in smooth generative pushforward models, such as in VAEs and GANs. For a generator/decoder $g:Z\to X$ and factorised prior $p(z)=\prod_i p_i(z_i)$, we define disentanglement as factorisation of the pushforward density $p_Î¼= g_\#p$ into one-dimensional "seam" factors, where each latent dimension controls an independent generative factor of the data. We prove that $p_Î¼$ factorises according to the SVD of $g$'s Jacobian; that disentanglement equates to two conditions on $g$ (C1-C2); and that under those conditions the seam factors are identifiable, up to permutation and sign. In the particular case of Gaussian ($Î²$-)VAEs, we show via an identity how diagonal posteriors promote C1-C2, in expectation, explaining why disentanglement arises modulated by $Î²$. Experiments illustrate this mechanism on Gaussian data, dSprites, and CelebA.
